candidates.name: Pemphigus vulgaris
support_spans: painful, erosive lesion around the stoma on the anterior abdominal wall
suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis
intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis
candidates.why: The presence of suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis and intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout the epidermis is consistent with Pemphigus vulgaris.

candidates.name: Pyoderma gangrenosum
support_spans: painful, erosive lesion around the stoma on the anterior abdominal wall
contradict_spans: No additional cutaneous or mucosal lesions were present
candidates.why: The presence of a painful, erosive lesion around the stoma could be consistent with Pyoderma gangrenosum, but the lack of additional lesions makes it less likely.

candidates.name: Pemphigus vulgaris
support_spans: high level of IgG autoantibodies: Against desmoglein 1: 40 IU/mL (normal value: 20 U/mL)
Against desmoglein 3: 90 IU/mL (normal value: 20 U/mL)
candidates.why: The presence of high levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and 3 is consistent with the autoimmune mechanism of Pemphigus vulgaris.

candidates.name: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
support_spans: high level of IgG autoantibodies
contradict_spans: No additional cutaneous or mucosal lesions were present
candidates.why: The presence of high levels of IgG autoantibodies could be consistent with Paraneoplastic pemphigus, but the lack of additional lesions and no mention of underlying cancer makes it less likely.

candidates.name: Pemphigus vulgaris
support_spans: Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin showed intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis
candidates.why: The presence of intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout the epidermis on direct immunofluorescence is a decisive finding for Pemphigus vulgaris.

candidates.name: Bullous pemphigoid
support_spans: suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis
contradict_spans: intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis
candidates.why: The presence of suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis could be consistent with Bullous pemphigoid, but the intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout the epidermis is more consistent with Pemphigus vulgaris.
